# Implementation Plan: Personal Link Collection

**Branch**: `001-personal-link-collection` | **Date**: 2026-05-12 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-personal-link-collection/spec.md`

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit.plan`. Phase 2 task breakdown belongs in `/speckit.tasks` (`tasks.md`).

**Re-run guard**: `.specify/scripts/bash/setup-plan.sh` always copies the empty template onto `plan.md`. On repeat `/speckit.plan` invocations, skip that bootstrap when this file already contains an approved implementation plan—or restore `plan.md` from version control immediately after running the script.

## Summary

Deliver an authenticated web app where each user privately saves **links** (URL, title, optional description), organizes them into **folders** (at most one folder per link) and **tags** (many-to-many), filters by folder and tag (combined filters use logical **AND**), enforces clarified rules for duplicate URLs, unique folder/tag names, and **default sort modes** (newest-first in the overall collection; alphabetical by title inside a folder context). Persistence and identities use **Supabase** (PostgreSQL + Auth); the client is **Next.js** with application data access through **Prisma** (pinned to latest stable minor at scaffolding time). Deferred: preview/thumbnail ingestion and alternate layouts (spec P4 SHOULD), native and messenger clients—as long as persistence and APIs remain evolution-friendly (**FR-008–010**).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript targeting **ECMAScript 2023** (exact `target`/`module` pinned by scaffolded tsconfig).

**Primary Dependencies**:

- **Next.js** latest stable supporting the App Router (**pin exact semantic version** when running `create-next-app`).
- **React** (bundled with Next).
- **Prisma** latest **stable** release + `@prisma/client` (per sponsor; pin in `package.json` at install time).
- **Supabase Auth** with `@supabase/ssr` (or current recommended SSR package) for session handling in Next.js.
- **Zod** (recommended) for server-side input validation aligned with Prisma types.

**Storage**: **PostgreSQL** hosted on **Supabase**; Prisma schema as source of truth for migrations; **Row Level Security (RLS)** enabled on user-owned tables with policies keyed to `auth.uid()` for defense in depth (see [research.md](./research.md)).

**Testing**: **Vitest** + **React Testing Library** for unit/component tests; **Playwright** for critical end-to-end flows (sign-in surface, create link, folder constraint, filters). Align exact versions with scaffold lockfile. **Per-phase policy** (TDD when practical, else tests immediately after implementation in the same branch before PR) lives in [tasks.md](./tasks.md).

**Target Platform**: Modern evergreen browsers; server runtime **Node.js LTS** matching Next.js requirements at scaffold time.

**Project Type**: **Web application** (single deployable Next.js app; no separate backend repo in v1).

**Performance Goals**: Interactive list operations (filter/sort) feel instant for collections on the order of hundreds of links on a typical laptop (no hard SLO—align with spec **SC-002/SC-003** validation scenarios).

**Constraints**:

- All collection data **must** be scoped per authenticated user (**FR-003**).
- Duplicate URL warning before persisting another user’s duplicate target (**FR-011**).
- Non-empty folder cannot be deleted (**FR-007**); folder/tag name uniqueness per **FR-012/FR-013**.
- Sorting rules **FR-014/FR-015** must be explicit in queries or application ordering.

**Scale/Scope**: Single-user collections in the **100s of links / dozens of folders** range for acceptance testing per spec; architecture should not preclude growth on Supabase/Postgres.

### Source Code (repository root)

Greenfield scaffold (not yet in repo)—proposed layout for the Next.js + Prisma + Supabase app:

```text
app/
├── (auth)/                # Auth routes / callbacks if split
├── (dashboard)/           # Authenticated shells
├── api/                   # Route Handlers where needed (auth webhooks, health)
├── layout.tsx
├── page.tsx               # Landing or redirect
├── globals.css

components/
├── links/
├── folders/
├── tags/
└── ui/

lib/
├── auth/                  # Supabase browser/server client helpers
├── db/                    # Prisma singleton, query helpers
├── validation/           # Zod schemas
└── urls/                  # Canonical URL normalization (duplicate warning)

prisma/
├── schema.prisma
└── migrations/

public/

tests/
├── unit/
├── integration/
└── e2e/                   # Playwright
```

**Structure Decision**: **Single-project Next.js App Router application** colocating UI, Route Handlers, and Prisma. No separate backend service in v1; future clients consume the same Postgres/Auth contract documented under `contracts/`.

## Delivery branching (implementation)

Specs and tasks use **delivery phases** (setup → foundational → stories → polish). Execution rule for code:

1. **One Git feature branch per delivery phase** (names in [tasks.md](./tasks.md)); branch from **`master`** (or from the tip of **`master`** after the previous phase was merged).
2. **Merge only via Pull Request** into `master` after:
   - the tasks for that phase are done (or deliberately scoped subset is documented in the PR),
   - **tests for that phase are done in the same branch** per [tasks.md](./tasks.md) **Per-phase testing**: prefer **TDD**; if TDD is blocked by real architectural friction, add automated tests **immediately after** implementation in that branch before the PR,
   - **the full automated test suite** configured for the repo passes (Vitest/unit, Playwright/e2e if present, lint/CI gate),
   - a short note in the PR links to the phase / task IDs (**Txxx**, **USx**) and, if applicable, why tests were not written first.

Long-lived **`001-personal-link-collection`** can stay for Speckit documentation; **implementation phase branches use ascending numeric prefixes `002`…`008`** (e.g. `002-phase-01-setup`, `003-phase-02-foundational`, …`008-phase-07-polish`; full list in [tasks.md](./tasks.md)) so branch order matches delivery order.

Agents do **not** commit or merge on your behalf unless you explicitly ask—you run `git`/GitHub flows locally or in CI.
